title: Reserved Pool Transitions: temporal quarantine and burst contract semantics
creator: Liam O'Connor
description: Product requirements for safe transitions between reserved pool states, introducing a temporal quarantine window and explicit burst contract semantics to reduce noisy neighbor impact and improve predictability for Dedicated tenants.
background: Customers using Dedicated pool reservations experience uneven performance when we preempt or reassign GPU slots during bursts or autoscale events. Current fallback and burst behavior is defined at high level but lacks precise temporal guarantees and an operator-safe transition plan. This creates flapping, rollback churn, and billing disputes for high-value tenants.
problem_statement: We need a clear, implementable PRD that defines: (1) a temporal quarantine during pool reassignments to reduce transient tail-latency regressions, (2) a burst contract that codifies what reserved tenants may consume beyond committed capacity and under what reclaim semantics, and (3) acceptance criteria and telemetry to validate tenant isolation and fairness during transitions.
goals: Define temporal quarantine semantics for reserved pool transitions (duration, allowed operations, telemetry signals)
Specify burst contract parameters: eligibility, rate limits, grace credits, preemption order
Ensure smooth operator experience: clear rollback and audit trail for transitions
Provide acceptance criteria and dashboards to detect regressions and customer-impact events
non_goals: Rewriting the autoscaler algorithm end-to-end (this PRD specifies interfaces and signals only)
Extending contractual billing changes for burst usage (billing will be handled by a separate initiative)
Introducing tenant-configurable quarantine durations in V1
constraints: Must be compatible with existing reserved pool metadata and routing policies
Quarantine logic should not add more than 5% steady-state CPU overhead on controller components
Changes must be reversible with a single rollout toggle
Target implementation fits into Dedicated runtime v2 API surface (no schema-breaking changes)
proposed_solution: Introduce a short 'temporal quarantine' state that a reserved slot enters during transitions (e.g., reassign, preempt, hot-rebalance). During quarantine: (a) new long-running requests are rejected or rerouted, (b) ephemeral burst requests may be served only if they fit within a short grace credit pool, and (c) KV/cache warmup is prioritized. Add a configurable 'burst contract' object on the reservation that defines max burst concurrency, grace credit rate, preemption weight, and decay window. Controller exposes transition audit events and trial telemetry for SLO evaluation.
user_stories: As an SRE I want to observe when a reserved slot enters quarantine so I can correlate customer latency spikes with lifecycle events
As a Dedicated tenant I want predictable behavior when my reservation is hot-preempted so my critical features degrade gracefully
As an oncall engineer I want a fast rollback path to clear quarantines if performance regressions are detected
As a runtime engineer I want clear signals (quarantine-enter/exit, burst-credit-debit) to tune the autoscaler
requirements: REQ-1: Temporal quarantine state must be defined with a default duration of 30s and configurable range 5-300s
REQ-2: During quarantine the router must avoid placing new high-priority long-running requests on the slot; short token-limited burst requests are allowed per burst contract
REQ-3: Burst contract fields: max_burst_concurrency (int), grace_credit_tokens (int), credit_refill_rate_per_minute (int), preempt_weight (low|medium|high), decay_window_seconds (int)
REQ-4: Controller must emit audit events: QUARANTINE_ENTER, QUARANTINE_EXIT, BURST_CREDIT_DEBIT, PREEMPTION_DECISION with correlation IDs
REQ-5: Admin console must show slot state timeline and recent audit events for the pool and tenant
REQ-6: Autoscaler integration: pool autoscaler must be able to query active grace credits and adjust scaling decisions accordingly

REQ-7: Default burst contract for new reservations must be conservative: max_burst_concurrency = 2, grace_credit_tokens = 1000, credit_refill_rate_per_minute = 50, preempt_weight = medium, decay_window_seconds = 300
REQ-8: Rollout toggle: feature must be controllable by runtime feature-flag and have an immediate kill-switch for emergency rollback
REQ-9: Add end-to-end tests that simulate pool reassignments with synthetic traffic and validate acceptance criteria
acceptance_criteria: AC-1: Quarantine enter/exit events are recorded with timestamps and correlation IDs in the audit log within 5s of state change
AC-2: During simulated quarantines with high long-request arrival rate, 95% of new long requests are routed away from quarantined slots
AC-3: Burst contract enforcement: when grace credits are exhausted concurrent burst requests beyond max_burst_concurrency are rejected with documented error code
AC-4: Autoscaler uses grace credit metric in at least one decision path in the canary rollout
AC-5: Console UI renders slot timeline and displays last 50 audit events without performance degradation
AC-6: Rollout toggle flips state across control plane & data plane within 10s during canary testing
AC-7: No more than 1 customer-impacting incident is triggered during closed-canary tests (internal tenants only)
rollout_plan: Phase 0: Design review and API contract sign-off with Runtime and Console (2 weeks)
Phase 1: Implementation behind feature flag; unit & integration tests (3 weeks)
Phase 2: Internal closed canary on staging with a small set of internal tenants; collect telemetry (2 weeks)
Phase 3: Gradual canary to 5% production reserved pools; monitor metrics and enable rollback guardrails (3 weeks)
Phase 4: Full rollout and docs update; enable public opt-in for burst contract overrides (2 weeks)
Rollback: immediate feature-flag off; controller will expire quarantines and return to previous assignment semantics
risks_and_mitigation: Risk: Misconfigured default quarantine could increase latency; Mitigation: conservative defaults and closed canary
Risk: Burst contract complexity causes tenant confusion; Mitigation: provide clear docs and UI tooltips in Console
Risk: Controller overhead; Mitigation: implement lightweight audit batching and ensure <5% CPU impact
Risk: Billing disputes for burst usage; Mitigation: surface burst consumption in billing dashboard (separate project)
Risk: Interactions with existing preemption policies; Mitigation: run integration tests with preemption matrix and adjust preempt_weight defaults
dependencies: ENG-439100: Console: slot timeline UI component
test_plan: E2E sim: create 50 reserved pools, trigger hot-reassignments, run synthetic mix of long/short traffic, verify AC-2 and AC-3
Load test: ensure controller CPU increase <5% at 10k quarantine events/hour
Chaos test: flip feature flag during high load and validate rollback within 10s
Integration: autoscaler consults grace credits and records decision traces
